title: Ella Langley’s ‘Choosin’ Texas’ Remains Most-Played Song on TouchTunes
summary: The 17-week Hot 100 No. 1 reigns on TouchTunes’ Q2 2026 ranking.
contentText:
Ella Langley ’s “Choosin’ Texas” isn’t just an ever-prevailing presence at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 — the song is also No. 1 for the second quarter in a row on the TouchTunes Frontline Chart for Q2 of 2026.

The TouchTunes charts for the second quarter of 2026 track the most played songs and artists on TouchTunes jukeboxes from April 1 to June 30, 2026, with the Frontline ranking inclusive of music released in the last 18 months, followed by the Catalog tally for any music that was released more than 18 months ago. The TouchTunes Artists Chart tracks the same period, combining an artist’s plays across both rankings. TouchTunes has jukeboxes in more than 60,000 locations worldwide. Its data is not factored into other Billboard charts.

“Choosin’ Texas” debuted at No. 2 on Frontline’s fourth-quarter 2025 edition before its Q1 2026 coronation , surpassing Morgan Wallen ’s “I’m the Problem,” which remains at No. 2 for the second-straight quarter. “Choosin’ Texas” was No. 1 on the weekly Hot 100 for much of the quarter and is currently at 17 weeks atop the list in all.

In fact, Wallen appears on the Frontline list five times out of its 25 positions, while Langley accounts for four. According to TouchTunes, plays of Langley and Wallen songs in the top 25 account for 57% of the top 25’s overall listens for Q2.

And while “Choosin’ Texas” remains at No. 1, it’s static only in positional ranking; per TouchTunes, the song rose 44% in plays quarter over quarter.

Langley even boasts two of Frontline’s top three this quarter, as “Be Her” zooms to No. 3 after a No. 23 debut for the first quarter with a gain of over 300%. Its success coincides with the song’s rise on the Hot 100; it reached a peak of No. 2 for two weeks (behind “Choosin’ Texas”) in May.

Wallen and Langley also remain Nos. 1 and 2 on the TouchTunes Artists Chart; Wallen has held the top spot since the ranking’s 2025 inception.

One other song joins “Be Her” as newcomers to Frontline’s top 10: T.I. ’s “Let ‘Em Know,” which leaps 10 positions to No. 10 in its second quarter on the survey. The song reached a peak of No. 33 on the Hot 100 in April, the rapper’s highest-charting song in over a decade.

Hip-hop also represents Frontline’s top debut of the quarter: Drake ’s “Janice STFU,” which bows at No. 12. That’s despite not being available for the full quarter, as the two-week Hot 100 No. 1 was released on May 19 as part of Iceman , one of Drake’s three albums premiered that day.

Though “Janice STFU” is Drake’s only appearance on Frontline or the TouchTunes Catalog Chart this quarter, he does reenter the Artists list at No. 4 as a result of the uptick in plays.

Chris Stapleton ’s “Tennessee Whiskey” remains at No. 1 on Catalog for a second quarter in a row, followed by Shaboozey ’s “A Bar Song (Tipsy),” the preceding ruler. Langley’s now in the top five there as well; “You Look Like You Love Me,” a duet with Riley Green , lifts three spots to No. 5.

Rock remains the top-performing genre on the Catalog front, albeit at 40% for Q2, down 1%. Country, meanwhile, rises as the Frontline’s top genre: 45%, up from 41% in Q1.
